title: ServePath Latency Cohort Inspector: streaming vs non-stream decomposition with tracehook enrichment
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a ServePath-focused latency investigation dashboard (cohort inspector) that exposes p50/p95/p99 and tail shapes by model and route, with an explicit split between streaming and non-streaming I/O modes. Enrich traces with new tracehook annotations (serve_path, kv_cache_hit, batching_window_ms, io_mode) so that dashboard panels and filters can correlate latency spikes with kernel scheduling, batching behavior, and cache/miss patterns. Ensure parity between metrics and logs pipelines: histogram rollups in metrics and percentile synthesis from request logs should match within tolerance. Provide drilldowns to linked traces and a lightweight playback for representative conversation shapes.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard shows p50/p95/p99 for a selected model+route and selectable time window
Dashboard exposes explicit streaming vs non-streaming toggle and shows both split and combined views
Tracehook annotations are present for 95% of sampled traces and appear as columns/filters in the dashboard
Metrics-based percentiles and log-derived percentiles agree within 5% for 1h slices on production traffic
Drilldown links open a trace in Trace UI with highlighted annotations and a link to the originating request_id
Performance: dashboard queries respond under 3s for 24h windows for typical selection, and <10s for 7d windows
Unit/regression tests for tracehook enrichment and CI job validating metric-log parity are added
implementation_notes: Work split into three parallel streams: (1) tracehook instrumentation in runtime (add serve_path, kv_cache_hit, batching_window_ms, io_mode) and sampling policy update; (2) metrics pipeline: histogram rollups by model/route/io_mode plus derived percentiles job; (3) dashboard panels and query templates in Console. Use existing tracing client lib to add lightweight annotations to trace spans to avoid payload blowup. For metrics, extend the existing percentile-aggregator to tag by io_mode and route; add SLO facets for streaming vs non-streaming. Use a Golden Dataset (1h production slice) to validate metric/log parity before rollout. Coordinate with infra for extra tracing retention during rollout window. Keep the trace sampling rate for problematic models at +10% temporarily via runtime flag.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge runtime PR behind feature flag and enable for internal org; 2) Deploy metrics job in staging, run parity validation against Golden Dataset; 3) Deploy dashboard to internal Console; 4) Enable feature flag for 10% of traffic for 48h, monitor parity and error rates; 5) Ramp to 50% then 100% if no regressions; 6) Postmortem & docs update. If parity >5% deviation during ramp, rollback metrics job and revert flag for further investigation.
testing_plan: Automated unit tests for tracehook serialization and a smoke test that asserts annotations appear in sampled traces. Integration test for metrics rollup using synthesized requests with known latency distributions. CI job that runs parity check daily for first week after rollout and alerts on drift >5%. Load test simulation for dashboard query latency using 24h and 7d windows.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: trace hook payload growth causing increased network cost and trace ingestion pressure. Mitigation: encode annotations as short ints/enums and use feature flag to control sampling. Risk: metric-log percentile drift due to aggregation windows. Mitigation: align rollup windowing and add correction factor in dashboard queries with documented provenance. Risk: increased dashboard query latency. Mitigation: precompute heavy aggregation in metrics pipeline and use cached tiles for popular queries.
open_questions: What should be the default trace sampling rate for models with extremely high QPS? (proposal: keep baseline 0.5% and +10% for flagged models)
Do we want io_mode to be an orthogonal tag (i.e., streaming=true/false) or encoded into route canonicalization?
Should the dashboard include synthetic baseline overlay (expected p95) from historical model profiles?
